$comment: Janitor known-junk registry. A file is junk ONLY if it matches a rule here. Every rule names its cause. Tier 1 = auto-trashable (provable accidents or regenerable). Tier 2 = tool-spray signature, trash only after verifying a real copy exists elsewhere. Tier 3 = suspects, report-only forever. Projects can protect MORE via .janitor-ignore; they can never loosen these rules.

exact_names.cause: Windows reserved device names created as real files on Linux — '> nul 2>&1' habit or cmd '^' line-continuation pasted into bash. Evidence: shelljs/shx#61; observed in ascenscion/client8.

dir_names.cause: Regenerable tool caches (same model as kondo's artifact registry).

contentless_files.cause: 0-3 byte files (empty, or '[]'/'{}') older than a day — failed queries that still emitted a file. Carries no data; trash is recoverable anyway.

tier2.cause: Tool wrote an absolute -output path as a flat underscored filename in cwd (certipy -output /abs/path behavior). Verify a real copy exists elsewhere before trashing.

tier3.cause: Suffix-cloned script variant (foo2.py) — the residue of an agent re-attempting a failed approach instead of editing in place.
Agent result scraps; superseded variants (res-probe2/3) common.
nmap -oA sidecar; keep the .nmap, this is the redundant grepable copy. Report-only: some workflows grep these.
